blue-catfish: Dan Megahan caught this large blue catfish in the Sassafras River.
Upper Chesapeake Bay Mark Hanson caught this large blue catfish while fishing live bait in the lower Susquehanna River.
Fishing at the Conowingo Dam pool continues to be good for a mix of blue catfish and striped bass.
flathead-catfish: Fishing with live bait in the lower Susquehanna River is a good way to fish for flathead catfish.
largemouth-bass: Largemouth and smallmouth bass are moving freely and feeding on a variety of baitfish and crayfish.
Largemouth bass also prey on crayfish.
Lures in the form of spinnerbaits , jerkbaits , tubes , and paddletails will entice both largemouth and smallmouth bass preying on baitfish.
smallmouth-bass: Freshwater Fishing Ronald Scribner caught this beautiful 21-inch smallmouth bass in the upper Potomac recently.
Largemouth and smallmouth bass are moving freely and feeding on a variety of baitfish and crayfish.
Smallmouth bass in particular focus on crayfish, so select your lures to mimic them.
striped-bass: These cooler water temperatures are making for good fishing for striped bass.
Anglers are reporting more bait schools are exiting the rivers and striped bass are holding along channel edges.
This is the fall jigging that every striped bass angler looks forward to.
walleye: The upper Potomac is providing excellent fishing for smallmouth bass this month, and walleye are becoming a greater part of the mix due to cooler water temperatures.
The lower Susquehanna River holds some large smallmouth bass and walleye, and few anglers know to target them there.
white-perch: Anglers who are targeting the large blue catfish have been known to use live bait in the form of bluegill sunfish or small white perch.
White perch are moving into the deeper waters of the tidal rivers as water temperatures drop.
White perch are also being found along the shallower sides of the bridge and are being caught on pieces of bloodworm.
